retained_passages.claim: Recordings support shared drive upstream of OMNs; integrator diffusion is a proposed source. Each cell was recorded separately in two animals.
retained_passages.reason: The actors remain distinct: the memory circuit supplies a command, OMNs activate muscles, the plant moves the eye, and the coil records it. Individual cell recordings cannot establish pairwise OMN covariance. Two animals are not replaced by a cell count.
source_checked: P2 Methods p9; P2 peer review p19

retained_passages.claim: Position, velocity, acceleration and fitted neural lead predict rate; the reported t test uses cells.
retained_passages.reason: All three terms have spikes/s units. A positive lead uses future movement in the forward fit and a delayed causal response in its inverse. Fitted m is correctly separated from anatomical mass. Test interpretation states its sampling approximation and cell versus animal limitation.
source_checked: P2 Eqs2-3, Fig1

retained_passages.claim: The inverse filter is a calibrated spike-to-position prediction, not an intervention on one cell.
retained_passages.reason: Factoring the quadratic gives the two stated time constants, identities and impulse response. Integrating across one spike gives a velocity jump 1/m. The area is 1/k, preserving physical gain. The example coefficient is 2.173913 and area 0.25; the equal-pole limit is correct.
source_checked: P2 Eqs4-7; direct algebra and numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Independent predictors obey sum R_i squared at most one; mean correlation 0.17 implies at least 0.0289 mean explained variance.
retained_passages.reason: Expanding the standardized residual proves the bound without equal muscle weights. The mean-square inequality is correct. Representative sampling and private-noise independence are explicit, so this does not silently turn single-cell records into a direct covariance measurement.
source_checked: P2 main p3; P2SI EqsS1-S2

retained_passages.claim: Covariance divided by movement variance estimates common displacement variance with unit common gain and negligible cross covariance.
retained_passages.reason: The decomposition identifies C as displacement after filtering, not a raw neural state. Large predictor noise lowers R without reducing chi. The constructed numbers give R=0.1700016 and chi=0.82. Weighted uncertainty is correctly limited to the error model rather than animal or calibration uncertainty.
source_checked: P2 Eqs11-17; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Independent position errors add twice their variance to positive-lag MSD, but zero-lag MSD stays zero.
retained_passages.reason: Expanding the squared difference produces the stated offset. The correlation-dependent alternative retains the covariance subtraction. A statistical correction is correctly separated from knowing trial noise. The constructed uncertainty is 25 percent of the corrected result.
source_checked: P2 Eqs18-19; peer review measurement discussion; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Decaying filters make stationary white-input MSD plateau; filtered Brownian command retains long-time growth.
retained_passages.reason: The covariance overlap and M=2[C(0)-C(lag)] are correct for the centered stationary output. In the Brownian example, it is velocity that becomes stationary. Integrating its exponential covariance gives 2D[lag-tau(1-exp(-lag/tau))], slopes two to one, and the quoted numerical slopes. The text limits its inference to the tested times and uncorrelated peripheral source.
source_checked: P2 Eqs20-22, Fig3; direct derivation; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Rates, saturating synaptic effects and a weighted readout close an approximate persistence loop.
retained_passages.reason: The equations match the primary model. X and S are dimensionless, each spike has the stated jump, and replacing spikes by their mean gives the saturating response. Summation gives tau_s E_dot=-E+G(E); exact persistence requires G(E)=E, with neutral derivative one and other stable directions. Approximate optimized weights are not called exact.
source_checked: P2 Eqs23-27, Methods p11

retained_passages.claim: The common stored position passes through motor filtering and the plant; delayed feedback changes the ongoing MSD.
retained_passages.reason: Motor output units and steady mean transmission are correct for active units. Counts of 1000 versus 2000 OMNs belong to separate simulations. The feedback has a negative velocity-like sign under the stated tracking approximation. A lag in a running process is correctly separated from time after a new perturbation.
source_checked: P2 Eqs28-35, Fig3; P2SI Extended Data Fig3

retained_passages.claim: Retaining every Mth Poisson spike gives CV=1/sqrt(M); the diffusion scale depends on what rate and slope are held fixed.
retained_passages.reason: The constant-rate interval sum and renewal count variance are correct. The information scale Na squared/lambda and 1/(tau_s squared J) distinguish absolute and fractional sensitivity. CV insertion is explicitly a scale estimate, not the full saturating network formula. The printed proportionality is not pronounced wrong from units alone.
source_checked: P2 Eq1 and sub-Poisson Methods; P1 Eq4; direct derivation

retained_passages.claim: Brownian changes of the represented state make only a small contribution to measured OMN CV.
retained_passages.reason: Subtracting expected squared time mean from expected time-averaged squared displacement gives DT/3. First-order inverse-rate expansion gives the stated fractional interval variation, about 0.002406. The arcminute-to-degree squared conversion is correct.
source_checked: P2SI EqsS3-S6; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: The full model supports one possible mechanism and does not uniquely locate noise in integrator neurons.
retained_passages.reason: The figure summaries distinguish observed correlations, reconstructed shared variance, internal simulated diffusion, and filtered model output. No integrator recordings or selective perturbation are claimed. Direct output-noise removal is correctly distinguished from removing internal stochastic drive.
source_checked: P2 Discussion and Figs1-5; P2SI Extended Data Figs1-10; P2 peer review pp12-13

retained_passages.claim: A fixed spatial Gaussian input is thresholded to produce connected fields.
retained_passages.reason: The random object is a map across space rather than a time trajectory. Joint Gaussianity, stationarity, isotropy and smoothness have separate roles. The threshold, gain and input scale are distinguished. Derivative variance is -C double prime at zero, giving the stated distance scale.
source_checked: P3 Eqs2-4; P3SI MethodsS1-S3

retained_passages.claim: Slope-weighted upcrossing density is exp(-q squared/2)/(2 pi sigma); an already active left endpoint adds Q(q).
retained_passages.reason: The narrow-band counting argument supplies the speed weighting. Height and derivative are independent by their jointly Gaussian zero covariance, giving the stated integral. Field counting convention includes clipped components and states the endpoint correction. No high threshold is needed for this exact mean.
source_checked: P3SI EqsS9-S15; P3 Eq8; direct integration

retained_passages.claim: Stationary field and gap means determine threshold and spatial scale; rare-field Poisson behavior needs long-distance decorrelation.
retained_passages.reason: The ratio is presented as a stationary per-component mean, not an exact expected finite-sample ratio. Inversion and the 200 m example compute correctly. The text states the extra independence condition and silent-cell selection correction.
source_checked: P3 Methods parameter inference, Eq5; P3SI S14-S15; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: At high q, mean peak curvature is -q/sigma squared and scaled excess height approaches an exponential law.
retained_passages.reason: Gaussian conditioning gives the Hessian mean; finite conditional fluctuations become relatively small. Peak selection and neglected remainder are explicitly qualified. The full width contains 2 sqrt(2), and rate versus linear width approaches exponent two rather than requiring finite-threshold data to equal two.
source_checked: P3SI MethodsS4, EqsS22-S25; P3 Fig3C-D, Fig5

retained_passages.claim: Transforming U=beta s to the power 2/d gives the limiting size density and moments.
retained_passages.reason: The Jacobian, beta units, gamma moments, Rayleigh/exponential/Weibull cases and integrable 3D divergence are correct. Limiting scale is kept separate from a finite-threshold fit. Direct PDF inspection confirms the supplement prints multiplication in S18, a missing sqrt(2) in S23, and a positive finite-height quadratic term in S25; the guide corrects those algebraic steps without asserting the data code shared them.
source_checked: P3 Eq1; P3SI printed pp12-14; source-check PNGs PDF pages13-15; direct algebra

retained_passages.claim: Restricting a spatial Gaussian field to a line or plane preserves its relevant Gaussian law, but field sampling changes.
retained_passages.reason: The restriction argument is correct. Counting slice components is distinct from cutting each original component through its center. Hit probability and off-center cuts prevent using the original radius distribution as an unweighted line-length law.
source_checked: P3 Fig2; P3SI FigS2

retained_passages.claim: A typical crossing has a Rayleigh positive-slope density independently of threshold.
retained_passages.reason: Slope weighting converts a Gaussian derivative into sigma squared v exp(-sigma squared v squared/2). Independent height density cancels. Rescaling the high-q crossing parabola recovers beta=q squared/(8 sigma squared). Finite differences are identified as rate-map measurements, not synaptic-input recordings.
source_checked: P3 Fig3E, Methods Boundary slopes; direct change of variables

retained_passages.claim: Euler characteristic is a signed component/hole count, obtained from signed critical-point contributions.
retained_passages.reason: The 1D, 2D and 3D signs, including a hollow shell, are correct. The Hessian determinant expectations lambda^j times b, b squared-1, and b cubed-3b follow from conditional covariance cancellation. The integrations give the stated Hermite factors. The underlying topological theorem is cited rather than claimed proved.
source_checked: P3 Eqs8-10; Taylor2006 theorem framework; direct Gaussian algebra

retained_passages.claim: Closed-box boundaries contribute additional terms; high-q component counts are an approximation to exact expected EC.
retained_passages.reason: Face multiplicities and normal sign factors give binomial coefficients. Rectangle replacements and periodic-boundary distinction are correct. Limiting checks and the negative cube value -20.05565 agree. The leading high-q count recovers the independent size-law mean. Additional firing cutoff uses q+t/a and the fitted rate gain is kept visible.
source_checked: P3 Eqs8-10; P3SI S16-S17; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Parameter fits and data processing constrain which comparisons count as further evidence.
retained_passages.reason: The table matches the primary Methods and captions, including conditioned 2D counts, 20-cell raw-map analyses, and histogram-only virtual-track fits. Skew and excess kurtosis use centered moments. In-sample comparisons are not called held-out forecasts. Threshold heterogeneity adds fitted parameters and shared cell properties without shared field locations.
source_checked: P3 Methods pp e2-e3, Figs1-5; P3SI FigsS1-S5

retained_passages.claim: Many independent random weights can yield Gaussian map values; spatial covariance comes from shared tuning profiles.
retained_passages.reason: The finite-dimensional vector CLT states normalization and no-dominant-input conditions. Covariance expansion uses the same weight at both positions. Uniform coverage, smooth profiles and independence supply different model properties. Gaussian profile autocorrelation widens standard deviation by sqrt(2), not two. Circuit uniqueness is not inferred from map statistics.
source_checked: P3SI MethodsS2, EqsS2-S8; direct covariance integral

retained_passages.claim: Fixed connection weights, changing unit states and the decoded remembered angle are different objects.
retained_passages.reason: The ring example allows the same weights to support different cued activity patterns. Defining working memory by later access avoids equating weight retention with ongoing cue retention or restricting all storage to persistent activity.
source_checked: P1 model definitions; stated constructed example

retained_passages.claim: Bits, capacitor voltages and PCM conductances represent different kinds of stored state.
retained_passages.reason: Charge, voltage, capacitance and conductance units and relations are correct. SRAM needs power, finite words limit representable levels, analog leakage changes dynamic voltage, and PCM can retain a weight while neural state vanishes. Device mismatch is separated from changing noise.
source_checked: Pehle2022 Sections2.1-2.3; LeGallo2023 SectionsI-II

retained_passages.claim: Digital states are updated numerically; analog currents change voltages; PCM reads multiply weight by pulse duration.
retained_passages.reason: The account identifies the variable that changes and the operation that uses it. The positive-contribution example Q=GVT has charge units, and signed handling is explicitly separate. Matrix operations are not equated with an autonomous recurrent memory.
source_checked: Intel2021 pp5-7; Scholze2026 Section4.4; LeGallo2023 SectionsI-II

retained_passages.claim: Feedback near balance gives tau_eff=tau_s/(1-g).
retained_passages.reason: Solving the single linear mode yields the stated decay, neutral and growing cases. The 10 ms examples give 1, 0.5 and 2 seconds. They are clearly illustrative, not measured chip performance.
source_checked: Direct linear ODE; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Restoring discrete dynamics and neutral continuous directions accumulate different local error.
retained_passages.reason: OU variance tends to D/kappa and its neutral limit is 2Dt. Its local scope excludes rare bit switches. Pinning can reduce variance while biasing cues. The neural diffusion bound is restricted to matching dynamics, noise and readout.
source_checked: Seung1996 line-attractor discussion; P1 model assumptions; direct OU solution

retained_passages.claim: Massoud demonstrates finite-resolution orientation activity; Giulioni demonstrates two-state persistence.
retained_passages.reason: The former reports 32 positions and 11.25 degree spacing with velocity updates. The latter reports high/low states, seconds of persistence and disturbance recovery. Neither establishes an exact continuous memory or Brownian law.
source_checked: Massoud2011 SectionsV.F-V.G, Fig21; Giulioni2012 Results

retained_passages.claim: Architecture and learning capability must be separated from a specific retention experiment.
retained_passages.reason: The table locates digital versus analog states consistently with the cited designs. BrainScaleS-2 acceleration is about 1000. Learning capability is not silently assigned to every application. Hardware calibration is correctly a setting adjustment.
source_checked: Intel2021; Scholze2026 Sections4.4,4.6; Pehle2022 Sections2.1-2.3

retained_passages.claim: Recent demonstrations address input history, deterministic persistence, adapted weights and storage-material drift separately.
retained_passages.reason: Kleyko implements history and nonlinear features. Aitsam reports 8 seconds, at most 0.5-cell movement, 15 percent less jitter, and an added 115 ms lag with worse tracking error. Ortner places non-matrix operations on a host. Wang separates optically programmed multiple levels from electrical switching and open array/endurance work. Those limits match the sources.
source_checked: Kleyko2025 hardware section; Aitsam2026 Sections2-4; Ortner2025 Methods deployment; Wang2026 electrical/optical demonstrations and Outlook

retained_passages.claim: Sun uses explicit slow state for input history; hardware claims are post-layout simulations; acceleration and messaging need physical-time accounting.
retained_passages.reason: The source identifies LMU-like slow state, successive register slots and offline training. The one-number model is clearly simpler than the source design. Its decay time is -delta_t/log(alpha), about 0.9995 seconds here. Four-chip communication evidence is correctly limited to that prototype.
source_checked: Sun2026 Fig4 and Methods; Ilmberger2025 SectionsIII-V; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Repeated cue trials estimate local mean drift and diffusion while checking writing and readout errors.
retained_passages.reason: Cue, decoder access, fixed weights, delay and angular wrapping are specified. The local Itô-style moment interpretation needs nearly constant coefficients, while long delays require circular statistics. Independent readout errors produce the stated intercept. These are proposed tests, not prior chip results.
source_checked: Direct SDE moments; eye-noise derivation; protocol explicitly proposed

retained_passages.claim: Projected temporal noise sets local angle diffusion; fixed mismatch changes deterministic dynamics.
retained_passages.reason: Normalized left neutral projection gives D=one half ell transpose B B transpose ell. It is not generally the visible tangent. Curvature and state-dependent drift limits are explicit. The example distinguishes lower variance from worse mean squared error, 4 versus 10 degrees squared.
source_checked: P1 projection framework; direct covariance calculation; numerical-checks.json

retained_passages.claim: Comparison requires matched model, output filter, readout, time and energy boundary.
retained_passages.reason: Spatial field statistics alone cannot establish temporal retention. If model time=a physical time, diffusion per physical second is a times model diffusion. The proposed energy measurement includes writing, waiting, reading and necessary host/interface work.
source_checked: P1 scope; P2 output filtering; P3 spatial-model scope; direct time substitution
